title: Shared dreams
description: Citizens report they all had the same dream

pitches.title: The Open House
pitches.text: Residents dream of touring the same beautiful house, then wake to find its owner waiting outside their bedrooms. Matching their descriptions leads investigators to a vacant property and the ghost of an estate agent who can only show it to sleeping buyers. He has been appearing afterward to ask whether they have considered an offer. Investigators arrange a sale to a buyer who died before exchanging contracts; both ghosts immediately insist the other pay for the roof.

pitches.title: Mandatory Training
pitches.text: Everyone dreams of working an overnight shift in the same factory and wakes exhausted. Investigators identify the machines from an old photograph and find the dead foreman still assigning work inside people's dreams. He insists production must continue, although the factory closed decades ago. Showing him the last batch of unsold merchandise finally stops the shifts; former employees complain that management waited until death to admit there was no demand.

pitches.title: Sleeping with the Enemy
pitches.text: Residents share a nightmare in which a huge creature chases them through town, but each night's chase becomes shorter. Investigators find the exhausted creature hiding in a condemned house: it feeds on fear through dreams and has picked a town whose residents mostly resent being woken up. They suggest showing it to the local horror club, whose members volunteer to dream about it. The creature gets fed, but the club starts demanding better pacing and a less predictable ending.

pitches.title: The Last Audience
pitches.text: Citizens dream of sitting through the same dreadful play and cannot wake until the curtain falls. Investigators recognize the stage as a demolished theater, where a dead actor has been summoning sleepers to his long-delayed farewell performance. He refuses to retire without a standing ovation. The team tells the audience what will get them home, and the actor leaves convinced his final performance was his best; everyone agrees it was his best because it was his final performance.

pitches.title: Dream Home
pitches.text: Neighbors all dream they are living the same man's comfortable life and begin accusing him of concealing a fortune. Following details from the dreams, investigators find an ordinary pensioner whose experimental sleep device is broadcasting his fantasies to nearby houses. His actual home is shabby, and he is furious that even his imaginary swimming pool now has neighbors in it. Disconnecting the transmitter restores private dreams; the neighbors remain convinced he has simply moved the money.

title: Deep hum
description: A hum can be heard with an unknown source

pitches.title: Idle Engine
pitches.text: A deep hum shakes nearby houses every night, despite the power company shutting off the block. Investigators trace it to a van behind a garage and discover an alien hiding inside a human disguise, keeping its spacecraft running while waiting for a passenger. The passenger has been dead for forty years, but the driver insists leaving would cost it a five-star rating. The team produces the obituary, and the alien departs after rating its passenger as a no-show.

pitches.title: Quiet Enjoyment
pitches.text: An apartment building vibrates with a hum that gets louder whenever anyone bangs on a wall. Following the vibration leads investigators to an enormous burrowing creature asleep beneath the foundations, purring whenever the residents scratch its ceiling. The increasingly desperate noise complaints have been keeping it delighted and awake. When the tenants stop banging, it falls silent; the landlord immediately claims his soundproofing repairs worked.

pitches.title: The Missing Bass
pitches.text: A low note sounds across town every evening, while a local musician's bass amplifier produces nothing. Investigators discover that his secondhand amplifier projects sound from its matching cabinet, which is buried under an abandoned dance hall. The owner kept turning up the volume because he could not hear himself practicing. Recovering the cabinet ends the mystery, but the neighbors ask whether burying both pieces would also work.

pitches.title: An Unfinished Tune
pitches.text: Residents hear the same low hummed phrase from empty rooms, over and over, with no final note. Investigators follow the first complaints to the house of a recently deceased singer and discover his ghost cannot remember how his favorite song ends. They locate an old recording and play it for him. He finishes the tune and departs, leaving his widow pleased that death has finally stopped him asking her to identify a song from three notes.

pitches.title: The New Neighbor
pitches.text: A neighborhood hums all night, and investigators notice that houses nearest the noise have stopped reporting termites. They find a vast insect behind a false basement wall, its wings vibrating as it eats through an infestation. The homeowner concealed it after realizing exterminators charged more and ate less. Moving it to an empty, infested warehouse ends the residential noise; the homeowner demands compensation for losing a service the investigators were called to stop.

title: Mysterious stairwell
description: People who explored the stairwell haven’t returned

pitches.title: One More Flight
pitches.text: People entering an office stairwell disappear, although calls from their phones say they are still climbing. Investigators discover that each landing repeats whenever someone decides the lift would have been easier; walking back down brings them safely to the entrance. The missing people have refused to turn back after investing so much effort in going up. The team retrieves them by announcing that the upstairs meeting has been canceled, and they complain nobody told them sooner.

pitches.title: The Perfect Tenant
pitches.text: Explorers vanish down a stairwell in a derelict apartment block, and investigators hear television sets playing beyond its bottom landing. The stairs lead into apartments preserved exactly as they were before a rent increase, where the missing tenants have voluntarily moved back in. The building's ghost keeps the rooms available because it misses having occupants. Everyone returns after discovering the same downstairs neighbor is there too, still practicing drums; the ghost admits it cannot make anyone stop.

pitches.title: The Long Way Round
pitches.text: Visitors enter a stairwell and fail to emerge for hours, then insist they only climbed one flight. Investigators compare watches and discover an antique clock on the landing slows time inside the stairs. A caretaker installed it so he could finish his cleaning before anyone noticed how long he took. Removing the clock frees the remaining visitors, but the caretaker wants the team to explain why everyone else's impatience should determine how quickly he works.

pitches.title: At the Bottom
pitches.text: Residents disappear down a stairwell that has begun descending far below its building's basement. Investigators lower a camera and find them seated around a subterranean creature, which has been imitating cries for help to lure company into its den. It lets anyone leave, but the visitors feel rude walking out while it is telling them about its day. The team brings a radio and retrieves everyone; the creature settles down to a call-in show and immediately becomes its most frequent caller.

pitches.title: The Staff Entrance
pitches.text: A sealed hotel stairwell opens, and everyone who explores it vanishes. Investigators follow it into the hotel as it stood fifty years ago, where the missing people are being put to work by a manager desperate to prepare for opening night. The stairwell is the only surviving connection to that single evening, and returning through it is easy once the guests discover where their belongings were taken. The manager objects to the sudden staff shortage; investigators point out that opening night was already a disaster and he is not going to improve it now.

title: Secret ingredient
description: Townsfolk are obsessed with the new restaurant

pitches.title: A Taste of Home
pitches.text: Diners claim the new restaurant serves the best meal their mother ever made, even when they order different dishes. Investigators discover a stolen enchanted spoon makes any food taste like the eater's happiest meal. The chef is using it to serve cheap frozen dinners, and the kitchen's former owner wants the spoon back. Returning it ends the enchantment; several customers keep coming because their mothers also served cheap frozen dinners.

pitches.title: Repeat Customers
pitches.text: Customers keep returning to the same restaurant while insisting they have never eaten there before. Investigators find the chef serving a mushroom that erases the memory of the meal but leaves the craving for it. He argues that the food cannot be disappointing if nobody remembers being disappointed. The team removes the mushrooms, and his regulars finally remember enough visits to ask why he has been welcoming them as new customers instead of giving them a loyalty discount.

pitches.title: The Compliments of the Chef
pitches.text: A restaurant has queues around the block despite serving meals that taste distinctly unpleasant. Investigators notice every diner leaves glowing reviews in exactly the chef's voice and uncover a cook using possession to enjoy his own food through his customers. He honestly believes his success proves he has finally found an audience. Breaking his hold empties the dining room; he accuses the investigators of sabotaging the business, although he was its only satisfied customer.

pitches.title: Reservations Required
pitches.text: Residents fight over tables at a restaurant whose food causes them to glimpse their immediate future. Investigators catch the chef sprinkling powder from a prophetic artifact over every plate, and find diners enduring terrible meals to learn tomorrow's lottery numbers. The visions only reach as far as the next meal, which is invariably another reservation at the same restaurant. Taking away the artifact breaks the cycle, and the diners discover the one prediction they should have acted on was that they would be wasting more money there.

pitches.title: Five Stars, No Substitutions
pitches.text: People who hate the new restaurant become its most aggressive advocates immediately after eating there. Investigators discover a bound spirit in the oven granting the owner's wish that nobody ever say anything bad about his cooking. The diners still taste everything and are getting furious at their inability to complain. Freeing the spirit restores their speech; the owner insists the subsequent reviews are suspicious because all of them arrived on the same day.

title: Unscheduled eclipse
description: An eclipse when there shouldn’t be

pitches.title: Shade Provided
pitches.text: The sun disappears over a single neighborhood while the rest of town remains bright. Mapping the shadow leads investigators to a backyard telescope whose occult lens enlarges whatever is placed in front of it into a barrier against sunlight. Its owner has hung a dinner plate there because the outdoor umbrella broke. Removing the plate restores daylight, and the neighbors who reported the frightening eclipse complain that the investigators have ruined a pleasantly cool afternoon.

pitches.title: The Longest Night
pitches.text: An eclipse begins precisely when a local night watchman is supposed to end his shift. Investigators trace the darkness to a vampire hiding as the factory owner, who has acquired a charm that prevents daylight reaching his property. He likes being able to work late and sees no reason the watchman should go home just because a clock says morning. Removing the charm restores the sun, and the vampire abruptly becomes much more receptive to a discussion of flexible working hours.

pitches.title: A Bad Omen
pitches.text: A cult announces that its ritual will blot out the sun, and an impossible eclipse arrives on schedule. Investigators find the cult delighted but unprepared: every member assumed the ritual was symbolic and nobody planned what to do afterward. The eclipse persists only while they continue chanting. Persuading them to stop restores daylight, but the leader insists the abandoned apocalypse should still count as a successful first event.

pitches.title: Reserved Parking
pitches.text: A black disk covers the sun, yet astronomy clubs outside town can see nothing unusual. Investigators track its shadow to a field and uncover an enormous alien ship using camouflage that hides it against the sky without hiding the sunlight it blocks. Its occupant mistook the empty field for a place to wait while visiting a relative concealed in town. Asked to move, it demands directions to somewhere convenient, and the team discovers that finding parking is apparently difficult throughout the universe.

pitches.title: A Moment of Silence
pitches.text: An eclipse begins during the funeral of a man who repeatedly claimed the sun would go out when he died. Investigators find his ghost holding the darkness over the cemetery, waiting for mourners to admit he was more important than they thought. A hurried eulogy satisfies him, and the sun returns. Once he has departed, the family asks whether the improved weather means they can finally be honest about him.
